Not sure what to do about a health concern? Healthline can help. 

📱 Call Healthline on 0800 611 116 to speak with a trained health professional for free, 24/7.  They can help you decide what care you need and what to do next. 

Find out more at healthnz.govt.nz/online-phone-healthcare/healthline
📱 If you live rurally and have a health issue but aren't able to see your usual doctor, you can call Ka Ora Telecare, 24/7, to talk to a nurse, free. Call 0800 252 672 (0800 KA ORA).

A recent rule change allows midwives to deliver more funded immunisations. By removing extra appointments and travel, more whānau are getting immunised sooner through trusted, familiar care.

Read more via RNZ: www.rnz.co.nz/news/health/...

content: 🦟 Extra mosquito monitoring is under way at Queen’s Wharf, Auckland. There is no current health risk, but surveillance helps prevent harmful mosquito-borne diseases. Help by removing standing water and not disturbing mosquito traps. If you catch or see an exotic mosquito, call 0800 669 943. #Mozzies

8 anti-seizure medicines in NZ now carry a new pregnancy cautionary advisory label — the first pharmacist added pregnancy warning of its kind. The label is designed to highlight the risks of taking certain anti-seizure medicines during pregnancy. 

Watch our videos on FACS below (links in comments).

media_refs.alt: Information graphic with a light grey background and a dark blue bell icon at the top. Large heading reads ‘ANNOUNCEMENT’. Below, text states: ‘From 1 April 2026, 8 anti‑seizure medicines will be subject to a cautionary advisory label, warning of the risks associated with taking them during pregnancy.’ At the bottom are the Te Kāwanatanga o Aotearoa New Zealand Government logo and the Ministry of Health Manatū Hauora logo

Information graphic titled ‘Example of the new cautionary advisory label’. At the top is a yellow warning label with an icon and text stating: ‘Talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding’. Below, text explains that the label will be applied to the following anti‑seizure medicines: Carbamazepine, Ethosuximide, Oxcarbazepine, Phenobarbitone, Phenytoin, Primidone, Sodium valproate, and Topiramate. At the bottom are the Te Kāwanatanga o Aotearoa New Zealand Government and Ministry of Health Manatū Hauora logos.
